title: Weekly paclitaxel for ovarian cancer · four visits per cycle
schedule_label: Paclitaxel over one hour on days 1, 8, 15 and 22 of a 28-day cycle. Day 22 is a treatment day unless your consultant specifically prescribes a different calendar.
schedule_summary: Paclitaxel over one hour on days 1, 8, 15 and 22 of a 28-day cycle. Day 22 is a treatment day unless your consultant specifically prescribes a different calendar.
purpose: After platinum chemotherapy has stopped controlling metastatic ovarian cancer, weekly paclitaxel can shrink or slow the cancer and help relieve symptoms.
indication_text: 00226b covers second-line metastatic ovarian cancer after failure of platinum-containing treatment. This weekly schedule is outside the Irish product licence.
administration_text: Paclitaxel over one hour on days 1, 8, 15 and 22 of a 28-day cycle. Day 22 is a treatment day unless your consultant specifically prescribes a different calendar.
monitoring_summary: Full blood count, kidney and liver function. Blood count, kidney and liver function. A full blood count is specifically listed for day 8. Symptoms, examination and scans according to your treatment plan.
review_status: Independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Paclitaxel
agents.explanation: Cells use tiny structures called microtubules to separate their chromosomes when dividing. Paclitaxel stabilises these structures so they cannot rearrange normally, interrupting cell division. It can also affect nerves and other healthy tissues.
agents.watch: Report tingling or numbness before the next weekly dose, especially if it affects walking or hand use. Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, chest or throat tightness, itching, dizziness or breathing changes during infusion.
risks: Sensory or motor neuropathy, potentially persistent
Hair loss and nail / skin changes
Rare serious lung or cardiac effects
consent_risks: Report numbness or tingling before the next dose.
Fever, shivers or suddenly unwell: call immediately.
Hair loss is common. Ask about scalp cooling before treatment where suitable.

sources.title: Gynecologic Oncology Group phase II study

common_effects.title: Hair and energy

common_effects.text: Report tingling, burning or numbness before the next dose. Trouble buttoning clothes or walking can mean the dose needs review.

serious_effects.text: Fever, shivers or suddenly unwell: call immediately.

support.text: Premedicines reduce the risk of an infusion reaction. Tell your nurse about any previous reaction and which medicines you took. Your team prescribes any changes.

support.title: Between visits
support.text: Call the 24-hour oncology number immediately for fever, chills, bleeding or feeling suddenly unwell. Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, breathlessness, dizziness, throat tightness or pain at the infusion site.

teachback: Show which days you attend, which medicines you take beforehand and how to contact the 24-hour team.
consent_support: The prescriber will discuss the medicines on your individual plan. Discuss the possibility of persistent nerve symptoms, infection, hair loss and a severe infusion reaction.
safety_note: Call the 24-hour oncology number immediately for fever, chills, bleeding or feeling suddenly unwell. Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, breathlessness, dizziness, throat tightness or pain at the infusion site.

evidence.title: Gynecologic Oncology Group phase II study
evidence.interpretation: Some participants with previously treated ovarian cancer had tumour shrinkage with paclitaxel.
evidence.limitations: This was a small, single-arm study. It cannot show a survival advantage or establish the best dose or schedule for you.

prescription_phases.label: Day 1 · Paclitaxel

medicines.name: Ondansetron
medicines.note: Review QT, constipation and hepatic dosing; reconcile any steroid already prescribed

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.dose: 10 mg orally up to three times daily as needed
medicines.timing: Subsequent days: duration to be confirmed
medicines.note: Assess contraindications, renal function and interactions

additional_support: First paclitaxel dose: dexamethasone 8 mg IV, chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV, each 30 minutes before treatment (NCCP suggested table).

From Day 8 onward: chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV 30 minutes before treatment. Routine dexamethasone may be omitted after the first dose; prior reaction or increased risk requires consultant review.
Famotidine may be omitted under the consultant/local plan if appropriate. A prior reaction requires a separate rechallenge assessment; do not reuse the standard draft automatically.
First-dose NCCP suggested premedication: dexamethasone 8 mg IV, chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV 30 minutes before paclitaxel.

From Day 8, dexamethasone may be omitted in the source suggested table; add or modify for increased risk or previous reaction under consultant guidance. Famotidine omission is also a consultant/local-policy decision requiring close observation.
The conventional paclitaxel product information has a different generic premedication regimen. Reconcile the exact product, weekly NCCP pathway and local policy; never self-omit premedication.
Low emetic risk; keep the antiemetic plan separate from reaction premedication. Consider analgesia for myalgia/arthralgia and early action on neuropathy.

guidance.label: NCCP antiemetic guidance; reconcile with regimen and individual prescription

prescription_phases.prescription_source: NCCP 00226 and NCIS medical oncology antiemetics
prescription_notes: Premedicines reduce the risk of an infusion reaction. Tell your nurse about any previous reaction and which medicines you took. Your team prescribes any changes.

local_adjuncts.directions: Rinse 1 mL around the mouth four times daily after meals during the chemotherapy regimen.
Rinse 10 mL around the mouth for at least 1 minute four times daily; expel after rinsing.
Take one tablet three times daily as required.
Take 4 mg after the first episode of diarrhoea, then 2 mg after each further episode, to a maximum of 16 mg/day.
